name: Russia
summary: The world's largest country and nuclear arsenal, waging a war of attrition in Ukraine on a war-economy footing. Under extensive Western sanctions, Moscow has pivoted energy exports to China and India and deepened military ties with North Korea and Iran.
strategicInterests: Secure territorial gains in Ukraine and prevent its NATO membership
Roll back NATO's posture in Eastern Europe
Circumvent sanctions and redirect energy exports to Asia
Dominance in the post-Soviet space (Belarus, Central Asia, South Caucasus)
Develop the Arctic and the Northern Sea Route

capabilities: Private and proxy forces in Africa (Africa Corps)

government.notes: Putin re-elected in 2024 for a term running to 2030.

resources.name: Natural gas
resources.note: Largest proven reserves in the world

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: Second- or third-largest producer; shadow fleet exports

resources.name: Wheat & fertiliser
resources.note: Largest wheat exporter; major potash and nitrogen supplier

name: Belarus
summary: Russia's closest ally, integrated through the Union State and host to Russian tactical nuclear weapons since 2023. Belarus served as a launch pad for the 2022 invasion and is under extensive Western sanctions.
strategicInterests: Regime survival and security guarantees from Moscow
Russian economic subsidies and market access
Sanctions relief through selective engagement with the West (prisoner releases)
Potash export routes

government.notes: Lukashenko has ruled since 1994; seventh term began in 2025.

resources.name: Potash
resources.note: Belaruskali is among the largest global producers

name: Kazakhstan
summary: Central Asia's largest economy and the world's top uranium producer, practising a 'multi-vector' foreign policy between Russia, China, the West and Turkey. It is central to the Trans-Caspian 'Middle Corridor' that bypasses Russia.
strategicInterests: Preserve sovereignty and balance great-power relationships
Develop the Middle Corridor trade route across the Caspian
Diversify oil export routes beyond Russia's CPC pipeline
Critical-mineral partnerships with the EU and US

government.notes: Tokayev's single seven-year term runs to 2029.

name: Azerbaijan
summary: A Caspian energy producer that retook all of Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023. Closely allied with Turkey and a major supplier of oil to Israel, Baku initialled a US-brokered peace framework with Armenia in August 2025.
strategicInterests: Consolidate control over Karabakh and finalise peace with Armenia
Open a transit route to Nakhchivan (the 'Trump Route' / TRIPP)
Gas exports to Europe via the Southern Gas Corridor
Strategic alliance with Turkey

capabilities: Turkish and Israeli drones and loitering munitions

government.notes: The Aliyev family has governed since 1993.

resources.name: Caspian oil
resources.note: Azeri–Chirag–Gunashli fields via the BTC pipeline

resources.name: Natural gas
resources.note: Shah Deniz supplies Turkey and southern Europe

name: Armenia
summary: A landlocked South Caucasus state reorienting away from Russia after Moscow failed to intervene in the 2023 loss of Nagorno-Karabakh. Yerevan has frozen participation in the CSTO and is pursuing peace with Azerbaijan and normalisation with Turkey.
strategicInterests: Sign and implement a peace treaty with Azerbaijan
Diversify security partners (France, India, US, EU)
Open borders with Turkey and Azerbaijan
Preserve sovereignty over the Syunik region

capabilities: Indian artillery and air defence purchases

resources.name: Copper & molybdenum
resources.note: Zangezur mine is the country's largest taxpayer

resources.name: Transit geography
resources.note: Syunik region sits on the proposed Azerbaijan–Nakhchivan route
